title: Pixels2Actions
hook: Can a robot learn flips by *imagining* them?
cta: How fast it learned: full episode, link below

segments.label: PAPER
segments.headline: A robot that rehearses flips in its head

beats.narration: Before trying a tricky move, people often picture it in their head first. So can a robot learn flips the same way?
Researchers at UC Berkeley first taught their robot's AI how its own body moves.
Then it practiced every move inside that picture of itself, like rehearsing in your head.

visual.sub: practice runs inside its learned picture of its own body

beats.narration: In the authors' tests, a leading rival failed every single flip. This one failed none.
And the moves it learned in its head worked on a real robot.

visual.credit: Video still: Liao et al., supermimic.github.io

beats.narration: The authors sum it up: trained in imagination, then straight to the real world.
These are the authors' own tests, on moves it had already practiced.

visual.sub: research paper · tested on moves it trained on
